set_1_petting_zoo: Hello. I'm Dracula. I volunteer here on Tuesdays. The goats know me. I know the goats.
Last week I organized the hay by softness. The rabbits approved. I cried a little. In a good way.
Kindness is a muscle. I exercise it daily. Six hundred years of reps. I'm very toned emotionally.
The new goat looked at me with its little goat throat and I felt..., ...famished. I said 'bless you.' It sneezed. I almost didn't let it stop.
We put me in group therapy. The other members are a werewolf who's afraid of squirrels and a ghost who's scared of quiet. We're doing great.
The goat sends me postcards now. From the other side of the fence. It knows what I almost am. It forgives me anyway. Goats are better than people.
set_2_the_soup: I bring soup to my neighbors. Homemade. I list the ingredients so they know what they're trusting.
Item one: pumpkin. Item two: more pumpkin. Item three is where it gets honest.
I've lived six centuries. You learn to feed people. It's the only immortal skill worth having.
The honest ingredient is that I can smell their blood through the walls. Through THREE walls, Karen. That's not kindness. That's a floor plan.
But I still bring the soup! Because the soup is real! The monster just walks alongside it! We carpool!

Karen moved. She said the soup was lovely. She said the sniffing was 'a lot.' Fair. Growth is two-sided. I left her a casserole at the new place. She didn't call the police. That's a five-star review.
set_3_the_mirror: You know what's underrated? Compliments. I give them freely. 'Nice coat.' 'Lovely teeth.' 'Great posture for a mortal.'
I'm working on it. The kindness. Every day. Six hundred years of practice and I still surprise myself.
My therapist says I should acknowledge the urge without becoming it. I said, 'doc, I've BEEN it. For centuries. I'm auditioning for something else.'
And then I saw my reflection in the spoon. And the reflection winked FIRST., I didn't tell my therapist that part. She has a nice face. I don't want to worry her.
So now I compliment the reflection too. 'Nice coat.' It says nothing back. That's progress. Monologues are just compliments with nowhere to land.
Being good is a practice, not a destination. The destination is probably a blood bank. But the practice! The practice is soup and goats and compliments to spoons. See you Tuesday.
